Hypothesis: In `toolz/functoolz.py`, the `memoize` function has a mutable default argument `cache={}`. Since this default dict is created once when `memoize` is defined and shared across all calls that don't explicitly pass a `cache` argument, every function decorated with `@memoize` (without specifying its own cache) ends up sharing the exact same dictionary object. This causes `double(3)` and `square(3)` to collide on the same cache key (`3`) and return whichever result was computed first.

Fix: change the default so each call to `memoize` gets its own fresh cache when none is provided, e.g. use `cache=None` as the default and instantiate `cache = {}` inside the function body if `cache is None`. This ensures each memoized function gets its own dedicated cache dict while still allowing users to explicitly pass a shared/initial cache via the `cache` keyword.
